extracted.intended_audience: individual researchers, teachers, and scholars (including independent scholars and faculty) preparing applications for the NEH Summer Stipends program
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing and submitting an application for the National Endowment for the Humanities (NEH) Summer Stipends program, including meeting eligibility, formatting, and narrative requirements and addressing the peer review criteria. The document is the NOFO specifying all program requirements, allowable/unallowable activities, submission processes, and review standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Period of performance — full-time two consecutive months
rubrics_metrics.description: Summer Stipends support continuous full-time work on a humanities project for a period of two consecutive months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Period must be two months long and full-time and continuous; may normally be summer months but can be at other times of year. Specified earliest and latest allowable start dates depend on the application deadline (e.g., for 2022 deadline: as early as May 1, 2023 and as late as September 1, 2024). Summer Stipends provide $6,000 for the two-month period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable uses of NEH funds
rubrics_metrics.description: NEH funds may support recipients’ compensation, travel, and other costs related to the proposed scholarly research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the stipend is paid through an institution, the institution must remit all NEH funds to the recipient and may not take an institutional allowance or claim indirect costs. See Funding Restrictions for unallowable activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding restrictions / ineligible activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Awards may not be used for specified categories of work and activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prohibited uses include: development of teaching methods or theories; research by students enrolled in a degree program (including dissertations/theses); training or coursework for the applicant; support for graduate student assistants; preparation or revision of textbooks; curriculum development; inventories of collections; writing guidebooks/how-to/self-help books; educational or technical impact assessments; promotion or advocacy of a particular political, religious, or ideological point of view or specific public policies/legislation; lobbying; projects falling outside the humanities (creation/performance of art); creative writing, autobiographies, memoirs, creative nonfiction; quantitative and/or policy-driven social science research. See D6. Funding Restrictions for the full list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible applicants and faculty nomination requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual researchers, teachers, and scholars are eligible; organizations are not eligible. Applicants holding tenured or tenure-track positions at institutions of higher education must be nominated by their institution unless exempt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citizenship: U.S. citizens (in or outside U.S.) and foreign nationals who have lived in the U.S. or its jurisdictions for at least three years prior to the application deadline are eligible. Currently enrolled degree students are ineligible (unless degree requirements are complete and conferral is pending with dean/chair letter). Institutions may nominate two faculty members per deadline; institutions must designate a single nominating official who conducts a fair and open competition. NEH will email nominating officials to confirm nomination and will declare applicants ineligible if nomination is not confirmed by the stated deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemptions to the faculty nomination requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Categories of applicants who may apply without institutional nomination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exempt categories include: independent scholars not affiliated with a higher education institution; U.S. citizens teaching at foreign institutions; non-tenure-track faculty; staff (but not faculty) at institutions of higher education (provided they did not teach during the academic year preceding the award); community college faculty; emeritus faculty; faculty at certain federally recognized minority-serving institutions (AANAPISIs, ANNHIs, NASNTIs, PBIs). Applicants claiming exemption must provide verification (Attachment 7) per instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concurrent and overlapping award restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules about holding other NEH and non-NEH awards concurrently with a Summer Stipend.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may hold fellowships or grants from other organizations (including sabbaticals and institutional grants) in support of the same project during the period of performance. However: you may not hold two or more NEH individual awards with overlapping periods of performance; you may not accept or hold two NEH individual awards in the same fiscal year; acceptance of an award in one NEH individual competition will prompt NEH to withdraw an application from another NEH individual competition in the same fiscal year. You may not work on a project supported by an NEH institutional award as a project director or participant during the period of an NEH individual award held full time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application submission method and registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications must be submitted electronically via Grants.gov Workspace or a Grants.gov system-to-system solution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A multistep Grants.gov registration process is required; NEH strongly recommends completing registration at least two weeks prior to the deadline and submitting the application 48 hours before the deadline to allow time to correct technical errors. NEH will not grant deadline extensions for lack of Grants.gov registration or password.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required application components and file naming
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific required forms and attachments must be included and named according to the Application Components Table.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required components include SF-424 (Application for Federal Assistance - Individual), NEH Supplemental Information for Individuals Form, Project/Performance Site(s) Location Form, and Attachments 1–6 (Narrative, Work plan, Bibliography, Résumé, Appendices, Degree conferral) with specified filenames (e.g., narrative.pdf). Missing required or conditionally required documents will render the application ineligible for review. Grants.gov may reject files with names longer than 50 characters or with disallowed characters. Do not include attachments other than those required or conditionally required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting requirements and page limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Attachments must conform to specified page, margin, and font formatting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General formatting: standard letter size (8.5 x 11”), at least one-inch margins on all sides, font size no smaller than 11-point, single-spacing, recommended fonts Arial/Georgia/Helvetica/Times New Roman. Citations are included in page counts. Specific page limits: Narrative — 3 single-spaced pages; Work plan — 1 page; Bibliography — 1 page; Résumé — 2 pages; Appendices — 2 pages (only for applicable projects). Images, charts, diagrams, footnotes, and endnotes are allowed if they fit within page limits. NEH will not review applications exceeding page limits or violating formatting instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative structure and content
rubrics_metrics.description: The narrative must be succinct, well organized, free of technical jargon, and follow specified section headings that align with review criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Name the file narrative.pdf and use these section headings: Significance and contribution (describe intellectual significance, thesis/claim, value to scholars/general audiences, relation to relevant studies); Organization and methods (describe methods, stage supported by stipend, chapter outline for books, overview for articles, technologies for digital projects, rationale for new translations when relevant); Competencies, skills, and access (explain qualifications, language/digital skills, arrangements for access to archives, plans for permissions); Final product and dissemination (describe intended audience and results, dissemination and access plans, publisher interest if any, implications of non-English products, URLs for websites). NEH expects the narrative to address the review criteria and to form a coherent whole.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work plan — content and expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: A one-page work plan summarizing the activities to be carried out during the two-month full-time period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Name the file workplan.pdf. The work plan should include a timeline of activities for the period of performance, be based on full-time commitment for two consecutive months (part-time not allowed), explain the part/stage of the project supported by the stipend, and discuss plans to finish the project if not completed during the funded period. Work plans should not depend heavily on factors beyond the applicant's control (e.g., receipt of outside reviewers' reports). If planning to submit a manuscript before the period's end, explain additional work required and why it merits support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bibliography, résumé, and appendices requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific expectations and page limits for these attachments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bibliography (bibliography.pdf) — 1 page; Résumé (resume.pdf) — 2 pages, showing qualifications and relevant experience; Appendices (appendices.pdf) — 2 pages and allowed only for editions, translations, database projects, and projects with visual materials. Appendices should include only material relevant to scholarly apparatus or visual materials; do not attach portfolios containing multiple PDFs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project title and project description limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Constraints and guidance for the project title and short project description (abstract).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Project Title: brief (no more than 125 characters including spaces), descriptive and understandable to the general public; avoid reliance on a subtitle. Project Description (abstract): written for a non-specialist audience, state importance and relation to larger issues in the humanities, and must not exceed 1,000 characters (including spaces). Exceeding the 1,000-character limit may cause Grants.gov to reject or truncate the description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters of recommendation policy and mechanics
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on reference letters, required contact information, deadlines, and restrictions on who may serve as letter writers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are encouraged to solicit two letters of reference; provide names, email addresses, and affiliations on the NEH Supplemental Information for Individuals Form (only one email per reference). NEH will email references two weeks after the deadline; letters should be submitted online by specified dates (e.g., Oct 14, 2022 or Oct 13, 2023). Missing letters will not disqualify an application, but late letters may not be considered by reviewers. Elected government officials, current NEH staff, and members of the National Council on the Humanities may not serve as letter writers. For translation proposals, one letter must be from an expert in the project language and should assess any translation sample.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review Criteria — Intellectual significance
rubrics_metrics.description: The intellectual significance of the proposed project, including its value to humanities scholars, general audiences, or both.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers assess how the project contributes to knowledge, its thesis/claim, and its relation to larger questions in the humanities. This criterion aligns with the Narrative 'Significance and contribution' section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review Criteria — Quality of conception, organization, and clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: The quality of the conception, definition, organization, and description of the project and the applicant’s clarity of expression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers evaluate whether the project is well-defined and well-expressed, and whether the organization and project description are coherent and persuasive. This aligns with Narrative sections addressing organization and methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review Criteria — Feasibility and appropriateness of the plan of work
rubrics_metrics.description: The feasibility and appropriateness of the proposed plan of work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers consider whether the stated activities and timeline are realistic and appropriate for the stated period of performance (aligns closely with the Work plan).

rubrics_metrics.name: Review Criteria — Applicant quality as an interpreter of the humanities
rubrics_metrics.description: The quality or promise of quality of the applicant as an interpreter of the humanities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers look at the applicant’s qualifications, prior accomplishments, language and methodological competencies, and capacity to carry out and communicate the project (relates to Résumé and Competencies section of the Narrative).

rubrics_metrics.name: Review Criteria — Likelihood of completion and dissemination/access
rubrics_metrics.description: The likelihood that the applicant will complete the project (not necessarily during the period of performance), including, where relevant, the soundness of dissemination and access plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers evaluate evidence that the project will reach completion and reach appropriate audiences, including realistic dissemination strategies, publisher interest, and plans for public access to digital outputs; this aligns with 'Final product and dissemination' in the Narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review and selection process expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: How applications are evaluated and how selection decisions are made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NEH staff first review eligibility, completeness, and responsiveness. Eligible applications undergo peer review by expert reviewers instructed to use the stated review criteria; NEH program officers may supplement reviewer comments; NEH staff make funding recommendations to the National Council on the Humanities and the NEH Chair makes the final funding decisions. Applicants may request copies of peer reviewers’ evaluations after public announcement of funded projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital products, public access, and maintenance expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Expectations for digital results produced with NEH funding regarding long-term availability and access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NEH expects that digital materials produced will be maintained to ensure long-term availability; applicants must describe how digital results will be maintained and supported beyond the performance period. NEH gives preference to award products that provide free access to the public and asks applicants to explain any plans requiring paywalls or other charges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright, NEH rights, and acknowledgment requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Intellectual property guidance for products created under NEH awards and requirements for acknowledging NEH support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients may copyright works developed under awards, but NEH reserves a royalty-free, nonexclusive, irrevocable right to reproduce, publish, or otherwise use the work for federal purposes and to authorize others to do so. All materials publicizing or resulting from NEH-funded activities must contain an acknowledgment of NEH support per NEH guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical file constraints and PDF requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical submission constraints for attachments uploaded via Grants.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attachments must be PDFs; convert non-PDFs to PDF and merge multiple documents into a single file per attachment. Do not use security-enhanced PDFs (password-protected, encrypted, digital signatures, XFA files). Converting to PDF may change length—ensure page limits remain within allowed counts. Grants.gov may accept applications even if required components are missing or incorrectly formatted, but NEH may later reject such applications as incomplete or nonresponsive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification for minority-serving institution exemption
rubrics_metrics.description: Documentation required to verify institutional eligibility for nomination exemptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants claiming exemption on basis of employment at a federally recognized minority-serving institution must include documentation in Attachment 7: Verification of exemption. Verification may include consulting the U.S. Department of Education Eligibility Matrix or providing a letter from the Department of Education certifying Title III/Title V eligibility dated in the appropriate year(s). Applicants must also confirm institutional enrollment-based definitions via NCES College Navigator if required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Degree conferral documentation for pending degrees
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements if applicant has satisfied degree requirements but the degree has not yet been conferred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have satisfied degree requirements and are awaiting conferral, you are eligible but must include a letter from the dean of the conferring school or their department chair attesting to your status as of the application deadline in Attachment 6: Degree conferral.

rubrics_metrics.name: Previously funded projects and subsequent applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules and review expectations for applicants who previously received a Summer Stipend.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Previously supported applicants may apply for a new project or a new stage of a previously supported project. NEH will evaluate previously supported projects with the same criteria but will ask reviewers to consider accomplishments from the prior award and determine whether the project warrants additional support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative, compliance, and reporting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Post-award administrative obligations including risk assessment, certifications, reporting, and compliance with federal policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selected applications undergo a risk assessment by NEH Office of Grant Management, which may request additional information. Applicants must comply with debarment/suspension certifications (2 CFR §§180.335 and .350) and NEH Research Misconduct Policy. Recipients must submit a Final Performance Report within 120 calendar days after period of performance ends; a final financial report is not required. NEH may impose special terms and conditions or terminate awards consistent with 2 CFR §200.340.
